parsed_answer.content:
In Apache Kafka, a consumer group is a set of independent consumer instances that work together to consume data from a topic's partitions. To guarantee that every message in a partition is processed by exactly one consumer in the group at any given time, Kafka must execute a coordination protocol known as a Kafka Rebalance. A rebalance is the dynamic process during which the ownership of partitions is reassigned among the active members of a consumer group. This ensures high availability and horizontal scalability, allowing the system to seamlessly absorb changes in cluster topology or processing capacity.

The rebalance protocol operates under the orchestration of a designated broker known as the Group Coordinator. Each consumer group is mapped to a specific internal topic partition (__consumer_offsets) based on the hash of its group ID, and the broker hosting that offset partition becomes the Group Coordinator. When a rebalance is triggered, all consumers temporarily pause their message-fetching loops and rejoin the group by sending JoinGroup requests to the coordinator. Once all members have checked in, the coordinator selects a group leader—typically the first consumer to join—which is then responsible for computing the new partition assignment strategy using a configured PartitionAssignor (e.g., Range, RoundRobin, or CooperativeSticky). The leader transmits this assignment back to the coordinator via a SyncGroup request, and the coordinator subsequently distributes the final assignments to all group members, allowing them to resume consumption from their newly allocated partitions.

Understanding when a rebalance happens is critical for maintaining low-latency event-driven pipelines, as traditional rebalances cause a 'Stop-The-World' effect across the entire consumer group where zero message processing occurs. A rebalance is triggered under several distinct operational scenarios: first, when a new consumer instance joins the group, scaling out the processing capacity. Second, when an existing consumer gracefully shuts down or ungracefully crashes, leaving its partitions orphaned. Third, when a consumer fails to send a periodic heartbeat to the Group Coordinator within the configured max.poll.interval.ms or session.timeout.ms thresholds, indicating a processing stall or network partition. Finally, administrative changes such as adding new partitions to a subscribed topic will also invalidate the current assignment map and force the coordinator to initiate a group-wide rebalance.

rows: High. All consumers revoke all partitions simultaneously before reassignment.
Minimal. Only partitions moving between consumers are revoked; others keep running.
Recomputes entire assignment from scratch across all members.
Incremental and iterative; preserves existing assignments to minimize movement.

items: The Group Coordinator manages consumer states using two primary timeouts: session.timeout.ms (the threshold for detecting total connection loss via missed heartbeats) and max.poll.interval.ms (the maximum allowable time between consecutive poll() calls, protecting against infinite processing loops).

During an Eager rebalance, consumers invoke their ConsumerRebalanceListener callbacks—first executing onPartitionsRevoked to commit offsets and flush states, then pausing until onPartitionsAssigned populates the fresh map.

Cooperative Sticky assignment mitigates the catastrophic latency spikes of Eager rebalances by executing multiple smaller, non-blocking rebalance phases until the cluster converges on the optimal partition topology without dropping unaffected message streams.

parsed_answer.content: A classic production trap leading to 'rebalance storms' is setting max.poll.interval.ms too low while executing heavy database operations or external API calls inside the poll loop. If a single batch takes longer than the interval to process, the consumer drops out of the group, triggers a rebalance, rejoins, pulls another batch, times out again, and repeats infinitely. Always tune your max.poll.records to ensure processing completes safely within max.poll.interval.ms, or offload heavy business logic to a separate thread pool while pausing partition consumption.

title: What is a Kafka Rebalance? When does it happen?
